plan.summary: This 1-4 block fits an off-camp 12-week build for boxing with only one S&C session per week and a higher sparring load. Week 1 establishes simple baseline performance with safe bodyweight tests that suit the available equipment, then Weeks 2-4 build lower-body power, upper-body strength endurance, trunk strength, and brief conditioning without adding too much fatigue to boxing. At the end of Week 4, review jump quality, push-up performance, conditioning recovery, and soreness before the next block.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general strength, jumping power, trunk strength, and repeat-effort conditioning with low-equipment work that does not steal from sparring.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the harder bodyweight strength variations and keep explosive work sharp while controlling fatigue from boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength qualities in place and express them with faster, sharper, lower-fatigue power work.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can with a quick dip and soft landing. Rest well between sets and stop if height drops.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best jump quality of the day and note if you felt springy or flat.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the quick dip in the countermovement jump feels uncoordinated.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable box if landing mechanics are cleaner than floor jumps.

exercises.name: Push-Up Assessment
exercises.reps: AMRAP stopping 1 rep before form breaks
exercises.notes: This set establishes your starting point for later progress. Use a straight body line, chest close to the floor, and clean lockout on every rep.

performanceTarget.prompt: Log your total clean reps so the next weeks can be matched to your current level.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up Assessment
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, box, or sturdy surface if floor push-ups are not yet clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up Assessment
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if incline push-ups are not available.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Control the step back, keep the torso tall, and drive through the front foot. Bodyweight only is fine if balance is the main challenge.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if stepping backward feels too unstable.

substitutionOptions.name: Step-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low stable step if knee comfort is better here.

exercises.name: Inverted Row Under Sturdy Table or Bar
exercises.notes: Pull the chest toward the edge or bar with a straight body line. Stop each set with 1-2 reps still in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if the setup is very secure and you can keep body tension.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if no safe row setup exists. It is lighter, so move slowly and keep the shoulder blades active.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, squeeze glutes, and keep ribs down. End the hold before the low back sags.

substitutionOptions.name: Body Saw Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if a regular plank is already easy for the full time.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot hold a clean plank position yet.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Keep a straight line from head to heel and do not let the top hip roll forward.

substitutionOptions.name: Bent-Knee Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the full side plank is too hard to hold well.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing Intervals
exercises.notes: Sharp conditioning only. Stay relaxed and fast, not sloppy.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump with max intent and land quietly. Take full rest so every rep stays crisp.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track whether your jumps feel faster and springier than last week.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the dip timing still feels messy.

substitutionOptions.name: Low Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you land better on a box than on the floor.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.reps: Submax sets leaving 1-2 reps in reserve
exercises.notes: Use the Week 1 test result to pick a hard but clean rep count for all 4 sets. Keep the body rigid and every rep identical.

performanceTarget.prompt: Use the same variation each week and try to add 1 total rep across the session without losing form.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor push-ups still break down early.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lower if regular push-ups are too easy.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Own the balance, pause briefly at the bottom, and stand up hard through the front leg.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if coordination is better without stepping.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if the regular reverse lunge is very easy and your balance is solid.

exercises.name: Inverted Row Under Sturdy Table or Bar
exercises.notes: Pull smoothly, pause at the top, and lower under control. Stop before the hips sag or the neck reaches forward.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only with a very secure setup.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Arm Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have a backpack you can load safely at home.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Drive through the heel, lock the ribs down, and finish with the glute rather than the low back.

substitutionOptions.name: Two-Leg Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the single-leg version cramps or shifts too much.

substitutionOptions.name: Hamstring Walkout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a harder posterior-chain option.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Press the low back gently into the floor and keep the hold tight, not shaky.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the full hollow hold is too demanding.

substitutionOptions.name: Tuck Hollow Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this as the middle step before the full version.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing Intervals
exercises.notes: Stay light on the feet and keep hand speed snappy.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Every rep should look explosive and clean. If the jumps slow down, end the set count there.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best-feeling set and note whether you are staying explosive across all sets.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the countermovement still feels inconsistent.

substitutionOptions.name: Pogo Jumps
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a lower-impact power option that still builds stiffness and rhythm.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.reps: Hard sets leaving 1 rep in reserve
exercises.notes: Use the same variation as last week unless all sets were clearly too easy. Keep full range and crisp lockout.

performanceTarget.prompt: Try to beat last week's total rep count by 1-3 clean reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if quality drops too early on floor reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a slower lower if you need more challenge without changing equipment.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a small rear-foot elevation only. Stay balanced, descend under control, and drive up hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the elevated version feels too unstable.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if setup space is limited.

exercises.name: Inverted Row Under Sturdy Table or Bar
exercises.notes: Keep the ribs down and lead with the chest. Make the angle harder only if all reps stay clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Arm Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have a safe loadable backpack.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorway Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only with a secure setup and no slipping.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.notes: Hold the top for a brief squeeze and keep the pelvis level.

substitutionOptions.name: Hamstring Walkout
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this for a tougher hamstring-focused option.

substitutionOptions.name: Two-Leg Glute Bridge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the single-leg version loses control.

exercises.name: Side Plank with Top-Leg Raise
exercises.notes: Stay stacked and do not let the waist collapse as the top leg lifts.

substitutionOptions.name: Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use the standard version if this variation is too unstable.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing Intervals
exercises.notes: Push the pace a bit, but keep the rounds technical and relaxed.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Stay fresh and explosive. End the jump work while it still feels fast.

performanceTarget.prompt: Compare this week to Week 1 and note whether your best set feels cleaner and more powerful.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it helps you keep the movement simple and crisp.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.reps: Submax sets leaving 2 reps in reserve
exercises.notes: This is a deload week. Keep the reps clean and stop well before grinding.

performanceTarget.prompt: Use this lighter week to see if the same variation feels easier than Week 2.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need an even easier deload option.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if regular reps are still very easy at the reduced volume.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.notes: Smooth reps only. Keep balance and leg control without pushing fatigue.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it feels more stable.

exercises.name: Inverted Row Under Sturdy Table or Bar
exercises.notes: Keep the pull strong and stop with clean form still in hand.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Arm Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the row setup is not available.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard and keep the hold smooth. This week is about quality, not fatigue.

substitutionOptions.name: Body Saw Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the standard plank is too easy even on the deload.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing Intervals
exercises.notes: Keep the work snappy and leave the session feeling better than when you started.
